title: melbfoot: Melbourne foot traffic
text: melbfoot helps people plan around foot traffic central Melbourne, café owners event planners, answer practical question: people walking past, much foot traffic changed since 2025? package contains data, two helper functions Shiny app: ped_hourly: average pedestrians per hour sensor, year type day (weekday weekend). ped_sensors: sensor . hourly_profile(): pulls typical-day pattern chosen sensors years. change_index(): compares year’s average daily traffic baseline year (earliest year data, 2025, default). launch_app(): opens Shiny app.

Sensor Locations dataset licensed CC 4.0. portal page counts dataset state licence, City Melbourne credited source throughout. raw hourly counts large, package includes summarised version: average pedestrians per hour, sensor, year day type. portal data start November 2024 run early November 2026, make years comparable package keeps 1 January 2 November 2025 2026. script data-raw/ped_data.R downloads raw files builds packaged data, process can reproduced.

title: Typical hourly pedestrian counts by sensor, year and day type — ped_hourly
Typical hourly pedestrian counts by sensor, year and day type — ped_hourly
text: data frame (tibble) one row per sensor, year, day type hour, columns: location_id Integer ID sensor location. Matches location_id ped_sensors. sensor_name Short name sensor location, example street mall name. year Calendar year (integer). day_type Either "Weekday" (Monday Friday) "Weekend" (Saturday Sunday). hour Hour day, 0 (midnight 1am) 23 (11pm midnight). mean_count Average number pedestrians counted hour, across recorded days group, rounded one decimal place. n_days Number distinct days went average. Small values mean sensor working part year, treat average caution.
